summary: claude-study-room is a Node/TS (tsx, no build step) "Protector" that keeps a warm pool of local Claude Code CLI "students" alive and dispatches them across roles (triage/implement/review/fix/rewrite/resolve/merge) against several GitHub boards at once. Operationally it is three process layers: a cmd.exe launcher (run-dashboard.cmd) -> a node tsx src/dashboard.ts HTTP dashboard on port 4700 -> a spawned ManagedProcess child running src/index.ts --live (the Protector engine), which itself spawns claude.exe students under cmd.exe /c (shell:true). Engine and student stdout is teed from the dashboard's in-memory ring to ~/.claude-study-room/engine.log (2 generations, 5 MiB each). Safety is layered and implemented almost entirely as pure, dependency-free modules that live.ts (2713 lines, the god object) wires: watchdog.ts (no-progress wedge counter, per-item attempt ledger, lifetime dispatch ceiling, board-churn detector), parole.ts (exponential-backoff release from quarantine), blackout.ts (nightly stand-down window), infraFailure.ts and capacityReset.ts (never charge an outage to an item), ciFailure.ts (classify a red check before dispatching a fixer), emptyRun.ts (an empty diff can mean "already done"), reportLifecycle.ts (retire watchdog reports whose item resolved), testRun.ts (bounded "finish N PRs then park"). The test suite is 70 files / 851 test blocks / 9855 lines run by node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts; the pure modules have genuine behaviour tests, but about 120 assertions across 14 files are source-regex text locks that readFileSync a src file and assert on its literal text. CI is a single ubuntu-latest job, so there is zero CI coverage of the Windows process/kill/exit-code machinery that is the entire durability story. One month of engine.log (34,834 lines, 2026-08-11 to 2026-09-11) shows the dominant failure modes are environmental rather than logical: 298 plan session-limit refusals, 119 "CLI returned no JSON result" (115 of them Bun segfaults in two 22:00-local bursts), 228 board-churn detections, and 84% of all lines being a 20s "Ingested N issues" heartbeat.

v2_implications: KEEP the pure-module layer verbatim - watchdog.ts, parole.ts, blackout.ts, reportLifecycle.ts, emptyRun.ts, ciFailure.ts, infraFailure.ts, capacityReset.ts, throttle.ts. Zero imports, roughly 900 lines combined, and every constant is a priced incident. Porting costs nothing; re-deriving costs months and six figures of tokens.

CHANGE: make process supervision an OS-level service from day one, not a .cmd restart loop. 61 of 76 launcher exits in dashboard.task.log are Windows session teardown and the daily recurring one is 0x40010004 (Ctrl+C / console closed). Ship the logon-triggered Scheduled Task (or a Windows Service, or an Electron tray app registered at logon) as THE install path, and delete the 'WMI is a durable stopgap' claim from every doc - it was tested twice and failed twice.

KEEP but generalise the teardown-vs-crash exit-code table (0xC000026B, 0xC0000142, 0x40010004) and the rule that teardown must NOT trigger a restart. A v2 supervisor that treats these as crashes will burn its entire restart budget in about 300ms, exactly as the old launcher did, because during teardown even the sleep primitive fails instantly.

CHANGE: separate the process that HOLDS state from the process that RUNS work. Today the dashboard owns the Protector as a spawned child and talks to it only through the filesystem (drain.ts, testRun.ts), so killing the console kills scheduling, telemetry and the only stop button at once. v2 wants a durable supervisor holding the ledger plus an ephemeral worker fleet that can die freely.

DROP the 20s full-board poll as the only clock. 84% of the log is the Ingested heartbeat - about 8,640 lines a day for two boards - and polling is also what drained the GitHub API rate limit (POLL_MS was raised from 2s to 20s in #62). Use webhooks or an event stream for board changes and keep polling only as a slow reconciliation sweep.

CHANGE: emit a structured event stream (JSONL with ts, level, event, repo, item, action, reason, cost) as the PRIMARY log, deriving the human line from it. Every question in this investigation required regex archaeology over prose, and 1,283 lines were double-counted because of an encoding split. Keep the rotating human log as a secondary view only.

CHANGE: stamp logs in UTC with an explicit Z and render local time only in the UI. logger.ts:10-12 prints UTC formatted as local while blackout.ts:45 reasons in true local - a 4-hour trap that made the 22:00-local crash correlation invisible until cross-checked against dashboard.task.log.

KEEP the outage-versus-item-failure separation as a first-class concept and make it the default rather than a patch. forgiveAttempt (watchdog.ts:251), isCapacityError, isInfraFailure and capacityReset together removed the largest cost sink in the log. A v2 dispatch ledger should charge an item only when a worker demonstrably READ the work; an unrun dispatch must cost nothing, including against the lifetime ceiling.

KEEP parole's cause-agnostic argument (parole.ts:1-24). Classification is a blocklist that forgives only what you have already been burned by, and the next novel failure condemns the board identically. Every parked state in v2 needs a time-based automatic exit, not just runner-error - today spec-changed and needs-human have none, and over 6,000 ingest lines show items sitting behind them.

CHANGE: one durable ledger, one writer. Replace quarantine.json + attempts.json + lifetime.json + handled.json + GitHub labels with a single transactional store (SQLite suffices) plus a projection to GitHub labels. The documented reset procedure - stop the pool, back up six files, hand-edit JSON, then a separate session to strip three labels - is not an operation v2 should be capable of requiring.

KEEP the lifetime ceiling and DROP the assumption that any other counter is monotonic. watchdog.ts:79-91 is explicit: attempts reset on release, parole's floor is about one dispatch a day which is unbounded over months, and only lifetime (never clamped on restart, watchdog.ts:418) makes 'forever' impossible. v2 must additionally add a BOARD-level and ACCOUNT-level spend ceiling - nothing in this engine caps total run cost, which is how one night cost 115M tokens.

CHANGE: bake a bounded / dry-run mode in from the start using testRun.ts's shape (finish N PRs or N merges, then soft-stop). Every expensive incident in the handoffs is an unbounded overnight run against an unreviewed change. Make a limit the default for any new prompt or policy and require an explicit flag for unbounded.

CHANGE the test policy: ban source-regex assertions (assert.match over a readFileSync'd src file) as a category - about 120 exist today and they pin shape, not effect. Where a text lock is currently the only option (staleDashboard, sharedCursor, tickReentrancy, webui), that is a signal the code has no seam: extract the behaviour into a pure function, as #140 forced for fairShare, or drive it through a real HTTP request against a started server.

CHANGE CI to run on windows-latest and to cover process lifecycle. An ubuntu-only job cannot reach taskkill /T, the teardown exit codes, the CRLF .cmd requirement, or the cmd.exe console-codepage encoding bug - exactly the class of defect that actually took the system down. Add an ubuntu+windows matrix and an integration job that spawns a fake child tree, kills it, and asserts no orphans remain.

KEEP the prompt-level classification directives (ciFixDirective, REVIEW_ROLE's required-versus-non-blocking split, the rewrite-versus-fix distinction) but treat them as versioned data, not string constants in a .ts file. CLAUDE.md's stale-triage section proves the failure mode: a prompt improvement does not retroactively re-run, and 87 issues kept a verdict from the old prompt for three weeks. v2 needs the prompt version recorded per decision so 'which items were judged by a superseded prompt?' is a query rather than archaeology.

ADD a liveness probe that proves the worker can do WORK, not merely that its binary exists. claude --version passes with an expired OAuth token (8 log lines of 401 OAuth access token has expired followed a clean preflight). Probe with a trivial real completion at boot and after every capacity pause.

ADD generic crash-burst detection instead of a hardcoded 22:00-23:00 window. blackout.ts is a mitigation fitted to two observed bursts and already missed the third (2026-09-01, 23:00-00:00 local). v2 should detect N failures of the same signature within M minutes and stand down adaptively, keeping a fixed window only as an operator override.

ADD per-worker budget stops from day one (cliStudent.ts:161 overBudget with maxTurns and maxTokens - 18 firings in the log, one at 8.1M tokens in 35 turns) and an idle watchdog (IDLE_TICK_MS 60s x 20 CONSECUTIVE silent ticks, counted consecutively so a laptop sleep does not massacre the fleet). Both are cheap and both caught real hangs.

DROP live.ts as an architecture. 2,713 lines holding a mutable per-board cursor (this.rs) across awaits produced the tick-reentrancy bug (both boards reporting the same five issue numbers as churn and parking a whole board behind spec-changed), the repo-qualification key mismatches (#153, #155, #148), and the untestability that forced the source-regex tests. v2 should pass board context explicitly on every call and make the orchestrator a thin, testable state machine over the pure modules.
